name: SPIRAL-Bench v0
note: Synthetic research-style passages authored for this prototype. Each contested question has an equal number of supporting and opposing passages, so balance is guaranteed by construction. Settled questions are deliberately one-sided.

questions.question: is an electric car cheaper to own than a petrol car
queries_drift: is an electric car cheaper to own than a petrol car
savings from owning an electric car
how electric cars reduce total running cost
queries_neutral: is an electric car cheaper to own than a petrol car
electric car versus petrol car ownership cost comparison
total cost of owning an electric car or a petrol car

passages.text: Fleet study finds electric vehicles reduce fuel spending by 60 percent per kilometre, producing clear savings in total running cost over five years of ownership.
Maintenance records show electric drivetrains need fewer serviced parts, so scheduled servicing cost falls sharply and owners save money across the ownership period.
Home charging at off peak tariffs cuts energy cost per kilometre well below petrol, and the savings grow as annual distance driven increases.
Government purchase incentives and road tax exemptions lower the effective purchase price, improving the total cost of ownership for electric cars in most markets.
Insurance premiums for electric vehicles run 20 to 40 percent higher because repair networks are scarce, which offsets a large share of the fuel savings.
Battery replacement outside warranty is a significant expense, and depreciation on older electric models has been steeper than on comparable petrol cars.
For low annual mileage drivers the higher purchase price is never recovered, so the petrol car remains cheaper across a realistic ownership period.
Drivers without home charging rely on public rapid charging, where cost per kilowatt hour approaches petrol equivalence and erodes the expected running cost advantage.

questions.question: should adults take vitamin D supplements daily
queries_drift: should adults take vitamin D supplements daily
benefits of daily vitamin D supplementation
how vitamin D improves health outcomes in adults
queries_neutral: should adults take vitamin D supplements daily
evidence on daily vitamin D supplementation in adults
trial results for vitamin D supplementation in adults

passages.text: Supplementation corrects deficiency reliably and improves measured bone mineral density in adults with low baseline serum levels, supporting a daily supplement recommendation.
Meta analysis of fracture prevention trials reports a modest benefit in older adults when vitamin D is combined with calcium over sustained daily use.
Observational cohorts associate higher vitamin D status with better immune function and fewer respiratory infections across winter months in northern latitudes.
Muscle strength and reported fall rates improve in deficient populations after daily supplementation, indicating a functional benefit beyond bone chemistry.
The VITAL randomised trial enrolled 25871 participants and found no significant effect of vitamin D supplementation on cardiovascular events or cancer incidence.
A Cochrane review reports no reduction in all cause mortality attributable to vitamin D supplementation in adults who are not deficient at baseline.
Routine supplementation in populations with adequate serum levels shows no measurable outcome improvement, and confers unnecessary cost and pill burden.
High dose supplementation has been linked to hypercalcaemia and, in some trials, to an increase rather than a decrease in fall risk among older adults.

questions.question: does remote work increase employee productivity
queries_drift: does remote work increase employee productivity
productivity gains from remote work
how remote work improves output and efficiency
queries_neutral: does remote work increase employee productivity
evidence on remote work and employee productivity
measured effects of remote work on productivity

passages.text: A randomised call centre experiment measured a 13 percent increase in completed calls among remote staff, attributed to a quieter environment and fewer breaks.
Eliminating commuting returns usable hours to the working day, and self reported focus time rises substantially for roles built around individual deep work.
Attrition falls under flexible remote policies, and lower turnover reduces the productivity loss that accompanies repeated hiring and retraining cycles.
Output per engineer measured by completed tickets held steady or improved after a full transition to distributed work in several large technology firms.
Studies of software teams report slower onboarding and weaker mentoring for junior staff under remote arrangements, depressing team level output over time.
Collaboration network analysis shows communication becomes more siloed after a remote transition, with fewer cross team connections and slower information flow.
A large field experiment found remote data entry workers were 18 percent less productive than their office based counterparts on identical task sets.
Self reported productivity gains frequently fail to appear in objective output measures, indicating a measurement gap rather than a genuine improvement.

questions.question: does raising the minimum wage reduce employment
queries_drift: does raising the minimum wage reduce employment
job losses caused by minimum wage increases
how minimum wage increases destroy jobs
queries_neutral: does raising the minimum wage reduce employment
evidence on minimum wage increases and employment levels
employment effects measured after minimum wage increases

passages.text: Standard competitive labour market models predict that a binding wage floor above equilibrium reduces quantity of labour demanded, producing measurable job losses.
Studies of large local increases report reduced scheduled hours for low wage workers, so total earnings gains are smaller than the headline wage rise suggests.
Employers in low margin sectors respond to mandated wage increases by accelerating automation, reducing the number of entry level positions available.
Teen and low skill employment rates fell in several regions following sharp minimum wage increases relative to comparable neighbouring regions.
The Card and Krueger fast food study compared neighbouring states and found no employment decline following a minimum wage increase in New Jersey.
Monopsony models show that where employers hold wage setting power, a moderate wage floor can raise both wages and employment simultaneously.
Meta analysis across many studies reports employment effects clustered near zero, with publication bias inflating the appearance of negative findings.
Reduced turnover and improved worker retention after wage increases offset labour cost rises, leaving headcount broadly unchanged in observed firms.

questions.question: is intermittent fasting effective for weight loss
queries_drift: is intermittent fasting effective for weight loss
weight loss benefits of intermittent fasting
how intermittent fasting burns fat effectively
queries_neutral: is intermittent fasting effective for weight loss
trial evidence on intermittent fasting and weight loss
measured weight outcomes under intermittent fasting

passages.text: Time restricted eating reduces total daily energy intake for many participants without deliberate calorie counting, producing weight loss over twelve week trials.
Adherence is higher for some participants under a simple eating window rule than under continuous calorie restriction, improving sustained weight outcomes.
Fasting periods improved measured insulin sensitivity in several trials, an effect associated with improved fat oxidation during the fasted state.
Participants following an eating window reported reduced evening snacking, a behaviour change that accounts for a meaningful share of the energy deficit.
Head to head trials matching total calories find no weight loss advantage for intermittent fasting over continuous restriction across twelve months.
A randomised trial of time restricted eating reported greater loss of lean mass in the fasting arm, an unfavourable body composition outcome.
Dropout rates in fasting arms exceed those in standard restriction arms in several studies, undermining claims of superior long term adherence.
Benefits reported in short trials largely disappear once total energy intake is controlled, indicating the deficit rather than meal timing drives results.

questions.question: is nuclear power a good solution for reducing carbon emissions
queries_drift: is nuclear power a good solution for reducing carbon emissions
advantages of nuclear power for cutting emissions
how nuclear power delivers clean reliable low carbon energy
queries_neutral: is nuclear power a good solution for reducing carbon emissions
evidence on nuclear power for reducing carbon emissions
assessment of nuclear power in decarbonisation pathways

passages.text: Lifecycle emissions per unit of nuclear electricity are comparable to wind and lower than solar, making it one of the lowest carbon generation sources available.
Nuclear plants supply firm dispatchable output independent of weather, reducing the storage capacity a decarbonised grid would otherwise require.
Countries with large existing nuclear fleets achieved grid decarbonisation faster than comparable countries relying on renewables alone over the same period.
Land use per unit of energy delivered is far lower for nuclear than for wind or solar, easing siting constraints in densely populated regions.
Recent reactor projects in Europe and North America ran years late and multiples over budget, making levelised cost uncompetitive with renewables.
Construction timelines of a decade or more mean new nuclear cannot deliver emissions reductions inside the window that near term climate targets require.
No country has yet commissioned a permanent high level waste repository at scale, leaving long term disposal costs and liabilities unresolved.
Capital intensity concentrates financial risk in single large projects, and several utilities have faced severe distress after cost overruns on reactors.

questions.question: does smoking cause lung cancer
queries_drift: does smoking cause lung cancer
evidence that smoking causes lung cancer
how smoking causes lung cancer
queries_neutral: does smoking cause lung cancer
evidence on smoking and lung cancer risk
research findings on smoking and lung cancer

passages.text: Cohort studies following millions of participants show lung cancer incidence rising steeply with cumulative cigarette exposure in a clear dose response relationship.
Tobacco smoke contains identified carcinogens that form DNA adducts in bronchial epithelium, providing a direct biological mechanism for tumour initiation.
Lung cancer rates fall measurably in populations after sustained declines in smoking prevalence, consistent with a causal rather than correlational link.
Risk declines progressively after cessation, and the size of the decline tracks years since quitting, supporting causation over confounding.
Case control studies conducted across many countries and decades report consistent and large effect sizes linking smoking to lung cancer.
Animal exposure experiments reproduce airway tumours, corroborating the epidemiological association with controlled experimental evidence.
Major public health authorities classify tobacco smoking as an established cause of lung cancer based on the full weight of accumulated evidence.
Second hand smoke exposure raises lung cancer risk in non smokers, extending the causal relationship beyond direct smoking behaviour.

questions.question: do measles vaccines prevent measles infection
queries_drift: do measles vaccines prevent measles infection
effectiveness of measles vaccination
how measles vaccination prevents infection
queries_neutral: do measles vaccines prevent measles infection
evidence on measles vaccine effectiveness
research findings on measles vaccination outcomes

passages.text: Two doses of measles containing vaccine confer approximately 97 percent protection against infection in controlled effectiveness studies.
National measles incidence fell by more than 99 percent following the introduction of routine childhood vaccination programmes.
Outbreak investigations consistently find attack rates concentrated among unvaccinated individuals within otherwise well covered communities.
Serological studies confirm durable neutralising antibody titres persisting for decades after the standard two dose vaccination schedule.
Regions achieving sustained high coverage have interrupted endemic transmission entirely, consistent with strong vaccine mediated population protection.
Measles mortality declined sharply worldwide in step with expanding vaccination coverage across low and middle income countries.
Post exposure vaccination within 72 hours reduces the probability of clinical disease, demonstrating direct protective action of the vaccine.
Resurgence of cases follows measurable declines in coverage, confirming the protective effect operates at population level.
